accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a hydro-meteorological disaster?
accepted.x: Cyclones are hydro-meteorological disasters. Earthquakes are geological, epidemics are biological and nuclear incidents are man-made or industrial disasters.
accepted.tq: Use the classification table to distinguish disasters by their governing natural or human process.
accepted.sec: Industrial and man-made disasters - Bhopal gas tragedy, classification of disasters  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Geological disasters — Earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
2. Biological disasters — Epidemics and pest attacks
3. Emerging disasters — Cyber attacks and space weather
4. Man-made disasters — Chemical accidents and nuclear incidents
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Geological, biological, emerging and man-made disasters include the examples stated respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each example with its disaster category before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Industrial and man-made disasters - Bhopal gas tragedy, classification of disasters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A widespread outbreak of a communicable disease such as COVID-19 is classified under which category of disaster?
accepted.x: Epidemics and pandemics, including COVID-19, are biological disasters.
accepted.tq: Test the category directly by identifying the underlying biological agent.
accepted.sec: Industrial and man-made disasters - Bhopal gas tragedy, classification of disasters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an example of an emerging disaster rather than a conventional natural disaster?
accepted.x: Cyber attacks, space weather and artificial intelligence failures are listed as emerging disasters.
accepted.tq: Discriminate emerging technological risks from geological, climatic and biological hazards.
accepted.sec: Industrial and man-made disasters - Bhopal gas tragedy, classification of disasters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Chemical accidents are regulated, among other provisions, under which pair of rules?
o: EIA Rules, 2006 and Bio-medical Waste Rules, 2016
Environment Protection Rules, 1986 and Forest Rules, 1992
accepted.x: Chemical accidents fall under the Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemicals Rules, 1989 and the Chemical Accidents (Emergency Planning, Preparedness and Response) Rules, 1996.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired legal instruments and their years without confusing them with environmental pollution rules.
accepted.sec: Industrial and man-made disasters - Bhopal gas tragedy, classification of disasters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the arrangements for chemical accidents, Crisis Groups may be constituted at which levels?
o: Central, State, District and Local levels
accepted.x: The institutional arrangement for chemical accidents includes Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups.
accepted.tq: Use the complete administrative-level sequence to avoid dropping the local or district tier.
accepted.sec: Industrial and man-made disasters - Bhopal gas tragedy, classification of disasters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The approach of disaster management in India shifted from a relief-centric approach towards which combination?
accepted.x: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 reflected a shift from relief-centric administration towards prevention, mitigation and preparedness.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy-direction change rather than selecting operational activities alone.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Policy on Disaster Management was formulated in which year?
accepted.x: The National Policy on Disaster Management was formulated in 2009.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the National Policy from the year of the Disaster Management Act.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 2(d) of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, a disaster is essentially a catastrophe that causes substantial loss beyond the coping capacity of the:
accepted.x: Section 2(d) focuses on a catastrophe causing substantial loss that exceeds the coping capacity of the affected community.
accepted.tq: Read the statutory definition precisely and identify the unit whose coping capacity is exceeded.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body)
a. NDMA
b. NEC
c. SDMA
d. DDMA
List-II (Head)
i. Chief Minister
ii. Union Home Secretary
iii. Prime Minister
iv. District Collector with an elected local representative as co-chairperson
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NDMA is headed by the Prime Minister, NEC by the Union Home Secretary, SDMA by the Chief Minister, and DDMA by the District Collector with an elected local representative as co-chairperson.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of NDMA and the Prime Minister, then eliminate incompatible codes.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: NIDM is associated with Section 42. Section 44 deals with the National Disaster Response Force.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect statutory section by comparing each body with its legal provision.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institution is primarily responsible for training, research and capacity building in disaster management?
accepted.x: The National Institute of Disaster Management performs training, research and capacity-building functions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the knowledge-and-capacity institution from response forces and funds.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to disaster management funds, consider the following statements:
1. The National Disaster Response Fund and State Disaster Response Fund are meant for relief.
2. The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are meant for mitigation.
3. The abbreviation NDRF may refer both to a response force and to a response fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The response funds support relief, the mitigation funds support mitigation, and NDRF is used for both the National Disaster Response Force and the National Disaster Response Fund.
accepted.tq: Separate response institutions from response funds and mitigation funds before choosing the combination.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For general States, the SDRF is funded by the Centre and the State in which proportion?
accepted.x: For general States, the Centre:State funding ratio of the State Disaster Response Fund is 75:25.
accepted.tq: Read the ratio in the prescribed Centre-to-State order and avoid reversing the figures.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Disaster Management Act, Section 35 relates to:
o: The constitution of State Executive Committees
accepted.x: Section 35 provides for hazard-specific plans.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the subject of the section from the bodies and forces created under other provisions.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which section is associated with disaster management plans of Ministries?
accepted.x: Section 37 concerns disaster management plans of Ministries.
accepted.tq: Use section-number discrimination, especially among provisions dealing with bodies and plans.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a feature of the Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2025?
o: Abolition of State Disaster Response Funds
Removal of statutory definitions relating to resilience and recovery
Creation of Urban Disaster Management Authorities in all Municipal Corporation cities, subject to specified exceptions
Transfer of NDMA chairpersonship to the Union Home Secretary
accepted.x: The 2025 amendment provides for Urban Disaster Management Authorities in all Municipal Corporation cities, except Delhi and Chandigarh, headed by Municipal Commissioners.
accepted.tq: Identify the genuine amendment feature while rejecting reversals and institutional substitutions.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2025:
1. It introduces statutory definitions of risk, resilience, recovery and evacuation.
2. It provides for national and state disaster databases.
3. It gives statutory status to the National Crisis Management Committee.
4. It makes a State Disaster Response Fund mandatory in every State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe features of the 2025 amendment. It also strengthens NDMA through audits and minimum relief standards.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of amendment provisions by checking each statement against the statutory changes.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who recommends the disasters eligible for notification, and who notifies them?
o: Finance Commission recommends; the Ministry of Home Affairs notifies
MHA recommends; the Finance Commission notifies
NDMA recommends; the Prime Minister notifies
accepted.x: The Finance Commission recommends the notified-disaster list, while the Ministry of Home Affairs notifies it.
accepted.tq: Apply the “who recommends, who notifies” distinction to avoid swapping institutional roles.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the notified-disaster list?
accepted.x: The notified list includes lightning, pest attack and fire, but no man-made calamity is included in the stated list.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded category by separating listed natural hazards from the expressly omitted man-made calamity.
accepted.sec: DM Act 2005 and National Policy on DM - bodies, NDRF, NIDM, funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the:
accepted.x: The Prime Minister chairs the National Disaster Management Authority.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional-political head associated with the apex disaster-management authority.
accepted.sec: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function associated with the NDMA?
o: Serving as the State Emergency Operations Centre of Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The State Emergency Operations Centre is run by APSDMA. NDMA lays down policies, approves the National Plan and provides policy for NIDM, among other functions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish national-level NDMA functions from the state-level operational role of APSDMA.
accepted.sec: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The overall coordination of disaster management at the Union level is undertaken through the disaster management division of the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The disaster management division of the Ministry of Home Affairs undertakes overall coordination.
accepted.tq: Identify the responsible ministry rather than the operational force or technical ministry.
accepted.sec: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about fire services in India:
1. Fire services are a State subject.
2. The Directorate General of Fire Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. Fire services have no advisory role in disaster management.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Fire services are a State subject, and the DG Fire Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards under MHA has an advisory role. Statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the false absolute statement and retain the two compatible administrative facts.
accepted.sec: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The southern campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
accepted.x: The southern campus of NIDM was set up at Kondapavuluru in Krishna district, pursuant to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
accepted.tq: Combine the institution, location and district to avoid nearby-place substitutions.
accepted.sec: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority?
o: It is chaired by the Governor and manages only post-disaster compensation.
It is chaired by the Chief Minister and functions as the chief nodal agency for disaster management in the State.
It is chaired by the District Collector and controls the National Disaster Response Force.
It is headed by the Municipal Commissioner and operates only in municipal corporations.
accepted.x: APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister, serves as the State’s chief nodal agency, runs the State Emergency Operations Centre and supports early warning.
accepted.tq: Match the authority with its chairperson and operational responsibilities in a state-level scenario.
accepted.sec: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The AP Disaster Management Rules associated with APSDMA were issued in:
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules are of 2007.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of the State rules from the years of the central Act, policy and Reorganisation Act.
accepted.sec: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following global disaster-risk-reduction milestones in chronological order:
A. Yokohama Strategy
B. Sendai Framework
C. International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction
D. Hyogo Framework for Action
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: The sequence is IDNDR (1990–99), Yokohama Strategy (1994), Hyogo Framework (2005–2015), and Sendai Framework (2015–2030).
accepted.tq: Fix the broad decade markers first, then place the 1994 Yokohama milestone within them.
accepted.sec: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction was the first concerted effort of the United Nations during which period?
accepted.x: The IDNDR covered the 1990s, specifically 1990–1999, and represented the first concerted UN effort in this field.
accepted.tq: Use the decade range rather than confusing IDNDR with the later Hyogo or Sendai periods.
accepted.sec: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Yokohama Strategy is best described as the:
o: blueprint that emerged from the IDNDR process
accepted.x: The Yokohama Strategy, adopted in 1994, was the blueprint developed from the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
accepted.tq: Identify the framework’s relationship with IDNDR rather than its date alone.
accepted.sec: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a framework with its period and principal emphasis?
o: Yokohama Strategy — 2005–2015 — resilience of nations and communities
Sendai Framework — 2015–2030 — succeeds the Hyogo Framework
accepted.x: The Sendai Framework covers 2015–2030 and succeeds the Hyogo Framework for Action. Hyogo covered 2005–2015 and focused on the resilience of nations and communities.
accepted.tq: Check both the date and the relationship or emphasis in each paired option.
accepted.sec: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priorities of the Sendai Framework?
o: Replacing national planning with international relief operations
Investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience
accepted.x: The four priorities are understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience, and enhancing preparedness for effective response and to Build Back Better.
accepted.tq: Recall the four-priority structure and reject the option that changes preparedness into an unrelated policy.
accepted.sec: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the seven global targets of the Sendai Framework?
o: Reduction of international cooperation in disaster management
accepted.x: The Sendai global targets include increasing the availability of and access to multi-hazard early-warning systems, along with reducing mortality, affected people, economic loss and infrastructure damage.
accepted.tq: Identify the positive disaster-risk-reduction target among reversed or unrelated policy statements.
accepted.sec: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which set contains the three post-2015 frameworks identified as shaping India’s disaster-risk reduction approach?
o: Sendai Framework, Sustainable Development Goals and Paris Agreement
Hyogo Framework, Kyoto Protocol and Montreal Protocol
Yokohama Strategy, SDGs and Convention on Biological Diversity
IDNDR, Paris Agreement and Ramsar Convention
accepted.x: The three post-2015 frameworks are the Sendai Framework, the Sustainable Development Goals for 2015–2030 and the Paris Agreement.
accepted.tq: Use the post-2015 time filter to eliminate the earlier IDNDR, Yokohama and Hyogo instruments.
accepted.sec: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks  [APPSC]
